document: R6-TRUTH-01. Documentation makes claims about WHERE a dependency comes from ('unmodified from crates.io', 'a soft fork consumed by path'). Those claims are only true if the RESOLVED cargo graph says so - a manifest line can say `registry` while `[patch.crates-io]` silently redirects the whole workspace to a path, which is exactly the contradiction the round-6 audit found. This file binds each documented claim to a machine-checkable assertion over `cargo metadata`'s resolve graph; tools/ci/check_dependency_sources.py fails when the graph contradicts the claim, and fails when a document still carries prose the graph has made false.

typedb.note: The STAGED product workspace: fork/typedb copied over the pinned upstream checkout. This is the tree every product build resolves, so it is the only tree whose resolved graph can settle a documentation claim about the product.

tools.note: The repo-owned spike/protocol workspace. It carries NO [patch.crates-io], so it is the lane where the registry crate is still the resolved identity - and documentation must not conflate the two.

claims.title: The product workspace resolves slatedb to the in-repo soft fork, not to crates.io
claims.why: sources/typedb/Cargo.toml carries a workspace-global `[patch.crates-io] slatedb = { path = "../../sources/slatedb-fork" }`, and fork/typedb/storage/Cargo.toml enables `external_epoch_required` unconditionally. Feature unification means EVERY crate in the workspace that links storage carries the fenced fork. A reader grepping storage/Cargo.toml sees `source = registry+...crates.io-index` on the dependency declaration and concludes 'crates.io' - only the resolve graph shows the patch.

claims.title: The tools workspace still resolves slatedb from the crates.io registry
claims.why: tools/Cargo.toml carries no [patch.crates-io]. The differential spike (tools/storage-diff-spike) deliberately measures the UNPATCHED registry crate, which is what makes it an oracle for the fork. Documentation that says 'the repo consumes the fork everywhere' would be false here, so the claim is checked in both directions.
